A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from DIG3D to LeanGaussian. All pages, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's Appendix A; v1 contains its supplementary analyses in the main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original ShapeNet reconstruction results, timing measurements, ablations and viewpoint analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 reports original ShapeNet and GSO results, timing measurements, ablations and qualitative evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The decoder changes from self-attention followed by deformable cross-attention to the reverse order, consistently shown in the prose, Figure 2 and update equations. The UNet/DINOv2 fusion, projected Gaussian reference points and multilayer refinement remain.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates category-specific ShapeNet cars and chairs. V2 retains these and adds Objaverse LVIS training with GSO evaluation across general object categories, plus qualitative testing on in-the-wild images in Figure 11.

E2.justification: V2 adds Hierarchical Splatter Image to the ShapeNet table and Triplane-Gaussian to the viewpoint plots. New comparisons include OpenLRM, Triplane-Gaussian and TripoSR quantitatively, and Gamba, LGM and InstantMesh qualitatively. The original ShapeNet table comparators remain.

E3.justification: The added Objaverse-to-GSO evaluation uses Zero-1-to-3 training renders, Free3D test renders and referenced splitting procedures, with four-day training on four A100 GPUs. A new restricted-view evaluation selects azimuth or elevation differences exceeding 45 degrees. Existing ShapeNet splits, million-step training and 100k-step ablation budgets remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds controls testing first-stage supervision and initialization from feature-extractor Gaussians (Table 5), direct encoder alternatives (Table 7), and distant-view robustness on GSO (Table 3). The original Gaussian-count, decoder-depth and opacity-filtering analyses are retained in Appendix A rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 newly reports averaging ten experiments and testing different random seeds during inference. V1 provides no corresponding run-count information. This is newly reported inference repetition, not evidence of additional training runs; no confidence intervals or variability estimates are added.

E6.justification: Reported ShapeNet PSNR entries change from 24.21/24.98 to 25.00/25.87 for cars/chairs. Timing and nearby-view-exclusion results also change, alongside substantial new GSO and qualitative results. V2's GSO 'Ours' PSNR differs between Tables 1 and 9, 22.36 versus 23.45, without an explained setting distinction, limiting interpretation of the exact scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the compositing count from all object Gaussians to Gaussians along the pixel ray. Equation 7 introduces explicit encoder, decoder and perceptual-loss coefficients into the written loss definition; LPIPS itself was already described in v1. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution is reframed from overcoming pixel alignment in category-level reconstruction to breaking both pixel and point-cloud correspondence constraints. The abstract and conclusion extend performance claims to open-category evaluation, while resolution-related efficiency becomes a prominent introductory claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations involving triplane rigidity, point-cloud modeling costs and resolution-dependent memory use, and contrasts its projection strategy with sampling in 3D. It also interprets the new supervision and initialization controls. Section 5 newly acknowledges difficulty reconstructing unseen textures and self-occluded regions.

D1.justification: V2 discloses Adam with learning rate 1e-5, downsampling kernel size 14, Xavier initialization and constant biases, plus Objaverse resources, render provenance and lightweight checkpoint selection. The abstract announces a future code release; it does not establish that code is already available. Existing ShapeNet details are largely relocated.

R1.justification: The positioning expands beyond Splatter Image's pixel alignment to point-cloud/triplane approaches and newer reconstruction models. Added discussions include Triplane-Gaussian, LRM, hierarchical splatting, Gamba and diffusion-assisted reconstruction, while DFA3D and BEVFormer provide new comparisons for the attention design.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten around LeanGaussian. Method subsections are consolidated and reordered, and experimental details and several existing analyses move into the newly organized Appendix A. This substantially changes the narrative beyond the method rename.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the introductory comparison and architecture figures, removes the visual-cone panel, and combines viewpoint metrics into a three-panel figure with shaded distant-view regions. It adds multiple comparison grids and tables, relocates retained point-cloud and sensitivity figures, and substantially changes text width, typography and page layout.

improvement.justification: Broader evaluation, targeted design controls and explicit limitations make the approach better supported and easier to assess. However, unexplained GSO score discrepancies weaken quantitative reliability. Moreover, v2 retains the claim of smaller degradation after excluding nearby ShapeNet views, although Tables 2 and 6 show a 0.58 dB drop versus Splatter Image's 0.21 dB; v1's corresponding figures supported that claim. These weaknesses temper the gains to a limited net improvement.
